decisions.decision: Minimum staffing hard-vs-soft is configuration, not code
decisions.rationale: ConstraintWeights is a @ConstraintConfiguration with persisted HardSoftScores, so min_staffing_weight decides the level. Defaults soft because contracted_hours_over is hard — a 9h shift span cannot tile a 13h window, so a hard floor on a thin day returns no schedule at all.

decisions.decision: Seat generation, not just a constraint
decisions.rationale: The constraint groups AgentAssignment by timeslot and a groupBy emits no group for an absent key, so it was inert on zero-demand hours at any weight. expandMinimumStaffingSeats guarantees a seat so the timeslot both appears in the grouping and has a variable the solver can assign into.

3.0 gave the +3..+5h window the user asked for and all 87 breaks complied, but 51 agent-days collapsed to 3-hour shifts (soft -258005) because contracted_hours_under is soft while breakBlockedWindow is hard. 4.0 pins +4h exactly; +3h is not expressible.

Standing preferences cannot express consistency: preferredBreakTime is an absolute LocalTime and honourPreferredStartTime only penalises starting EARLIER, so it is a floor not an anchor. Four-stage plan agreed, not started.
